title: Open cloze: the conference
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: Next week our company [1] going to organise a conference for two hundred developers. The event is [2] to start on Friday at nine. I think it [3] be a great success. By the time the first speaker arrives, we [4] have finished all the preparations. Please don't call me between 10 [5] noon on Thursday, because I will be giving interviews.

pat: our company es singular: is going to organise.
la estructura es be going to + verbo; will be no se combina con going to: is.
items.e: company = it → is going to.

pat: be about to = inminente; Friday at nine es un horario programado: due.
likely to = probable; el evento está programado: due.
items.e: Horario fijo (Friday at nine) → is due to start.

pat: I think + opinión sobre el futuro → will be.
items.e: 'I think' → will + base.

pat: By the time + plazo → Future Perfect: we will have finished.
items.e: By the time (arrives) → cláusula principal en Future Perfect: will have finished.

pat: el rango de horas se dice between ... and ...: between 10 and noon.
items.e: between 10 AND noon.

title: Open cloze: a new city
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: This time next month, I [1] be working in a new city. I am moving on the first of the month, so I will send you my address as soon as I [2] settled in. The company is [3] to open a second office there next year, and it is [4] to be very successful. By the end of the year, I [5] have met all my new colleagues.

pat: This time next month marca una acción en progreso en el futuro: will be working.
items.e: 'This time next month' → will be working.

pat: después de as soon as no va will; se usa presente (perfecto): as soon as I have settled in.
I → have: I have settled in.
items.e: as soon as + Present Perfect (I have settled in), nunca will.

pat: be about to = inminente; open next year es algo programado: due.
likely to = probable; es un plan programado: due.
items.e: Plan programado para el año próximo → is due to open.

pat: it is likely to be very successful = es probable que tenga éxito; due y about no expresan probabilidad.
items.e: Probabilidad → is likely to be successful.

pat: By the end of the year marca un plazo: Future Perfect, I will have met.
items.e: By the end of the year → Future Perfect: will have met.

title: Multiple choice cloze: a trip to Japan
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: Sam [1] to Japan next month: he has already booked everything. His plane [2] at 6 a.m. on Monday. He is sure that the trip [3] amazing. As soon as he [4] in Tokyo, he will call his parents. By this time next week, he [5] on the beach.

items.e: Ya reservado → arreglo organizado.

flies: el presente simple es para horarios; ya reservó todo (arreglo): is flying.
will fly: gramatical, pero he has already booked everything indica un arreglo organizado: Present Continuous, is flying.

items.e: Horario de vuelo → Present Simple.

will leave: un horario de vuelo (at 6 a.m. on Monday) se dice con presente simple: leaves.
leave: his plane es 3.ª persona singular: leaves (con -s).

items.e: 'He is sure' → predicción → will.

is being: el Present Continuous es para arreglos; he is sure introduce una opinión: will be.
is: el presente simple no habla de una predicción futura; he is sure + opinión: will be.

items.e: as soon as + Present Simple.

will arrive: después de as soon as no va will; presente simple: arrives.
is arriving: el Present Continuous no se usa acá; presente simple: arrives.

items.e: 'This time next week' → en progreso.

will lie: By this time next week es un momento exacto con la acción en progreso: will be lying.
will have lain: will have lain sería ya terminada; acá está en progreso: will be lying.

title: Multiple choice cloze: release night
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: By the time the client [1] tomorrow, the team [2] the last bug. We [3] the new version at midnight, so please don't call us then. It [4] to take about two hours, and we will not leave the office until everything [5] correctly.

items.e: By the time + Present Simple.

will call: después de By the time no va will; presente simple: calls.
is going to call: después de By the time no va going to; presente simple: calls.
called: pasado; la frase habla de mañana: presente simple, calls.

items.e: By the time → Future Perfect.

will fix: By the time marca un plazo: ya lo habrán arreglado → Future Perfect: will have fixed.
will be fixing: will be fixing sería en progreso; By the time indica que estará terminado: will have fixed.
fixes: el presente simple no marca algo terminado para entonces; By the time + plazo: will have fixed.

items.e: 'at midnight ... don't call us then' → en progreso.

will deploy: at midnight, y please don't call us then: a esa hora estarán en pleno deploy (en progreso): will be deploying.
will have deployed: will have deployed sería ya terminado a medianoche; acá está en progreso: will be deploying.
deploy: falta el futuro; en progreso a medianoche: will be deploying.

items.e: Estimación ('about two hours') → probable.

is due: falta to (is due to take) y due to = programado; acá se estima cuánto durará: is likely.
is about: falta to y about to = inminente; acá se estima cuánto durará: is likely.
is unlikely: unlikely = improbable; take about two hours es una estimación probable: is likely.

items.e: until + Present Simple.

will work: después de until no va will; presente simple: works.
is working: el Present Continuous no se usa acá; presente simple: works.
worked: pasado; la frase habla del futuro: works.

title: Gapped text: the launch plan
instructions: Cinco oraciones fueron eliminadas del texto. Elegí de la lista (A-H) la que encaja en cada hueco. Hay TRES oraciones que sobran.
text: Our team is preparing the launch of a new mobile app. [1] The developers are finishing the last features this week, and the testers start on Monday. [2] By the time the testing phase ends, the developers will have fixed all the reported bugs. Next month, the marketing team is meeting several journalists. [3] They will be presenting the app during a live event on 15 June. As soon as the event finishes, the app will be available in all stores. [4] The company is likely to reach its first thousand users in a week. Nobody knows for sure, though. [5] Whatever happens, the team will be watching the numbers carefully.
bank: The launch is due to take place in June.
The testing phase will be very demanding.
They have prepared a short video to show the main features.
Everyone hopes the reaction of the users will be positive.
Predictions are always difficult with a new product.
The old version was launched three years ago and was a great success.
The company was founded by two engineers in 2015.
The journalists decided to cancel the interview yesterday.

a: The launch is due to take place in June.
items.e: Introduce la fecha del lanzamiento; luego se detalla el trabajo previo.

a: The testing phase will be very demanding.
items.e: Retoma 'the testers start on Monday' y anticipa 'the testing phase ends'.

a: They have prepared a short video to show the main features.
items.e: 'They' = marketing team; el siguiente 'They will be presenting' continúa con el mismo sujeto.

a: Everyone hopes the reaction of the users will be positive.
items.e: Prepara la predicción sobre los primeros usuarios.

a: Predictions are always difficult with a new product.
items.e: Continúa 'Nobody knows for sure, though'.

title: Aviso de IT
instructions: Leé el mensaje y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text:
To: All staff
Subject: Server maintenance
The servers will be down for maintenance on Saturday from 11 p.m. until 2 a.m. While the work is being done, you will not be able to open the shared drive. Please save your files before you leave on Friday. — IT Team

o: Save their files before leaving on Friday
Come to the office on Saturday night
items.a: Save their files before leaving on Friday
items.e: 'Please save your files before you leave on Friday'.

Come to the office on Saturday night: los servidores estarán caídos el sábado; el aviso no pide ir a la oficina.
11 p.m. es la hora en que empieza el mantenimiento; no hay que llamar a IT.

title: Mensaje de chat
instructions: Leé el mensaje y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text:
Chat · Leo → Mia
Hi Mia, I'm meeting the client at 3, so I'll be presenting during the team call. Can you take notes for me? I'll send you the slides as soon as I finish them. Thanks!

items.q: What does Leo ask Mia to do?
o: Take notes during the team call
items.a: Take notes during the team call
items.e: 'Can you take notes for me?'.

Present the slides: Leo es quien presenta (I'll be presenting); Mia debe tomar notas.
Meet the client at 3: quien se reúne con el cliente a las 3 es Leo.

title: The big day
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta para cada pregunta.
text:
Tomorrow is the big day for Lucía's team. After eight months of work, they are launching their app at 10 a.m. Lucía has been worrying about it all week. "I'm sure everything will go well," she says, "but I can't stop thinking about what could go wrong."
The schedule for tomorrow is tight. The servers will be switched on at 9:30, and the team will be checking every system until the launch. If there are no problems, the marketing team will send the announcement to two thousand subscribers at exactly 10 o'clock. By noon, the team hopes to have reached its first five hundred downloads.
Lucía's manager has told the team not to work late tonight. "You will need all your energy tomorrow," he said. "Once the app is live, there will be plenty to do. When you get home, turn off your phones and get a good night's sleep."
Lucía isn't going to follow the advice completely. She is meeting her best friend for dinner at eight, and she will try to relax. But she knows that, by the time she goes to bed, she will have checked the servers at least three times.

items.e: 'launching their app at 10 a.m.'.

9:30: a las 9:30 se encienden los servidores; el lanzamiento es a las 10.
Noon: al mediodía se espera ya tener 500 descargas; no es la hora del lanzamiento.

items.q: What will the team be doing until the launch?
items.e: 'will be checking every system until the launch'.

Waiting for subscribers: antes del lanzamiento revisan los sistemas; el anuncio a los suscriptores se envía a las 10.
Sleeping: el manager les pidió descansar esta noche, no durante el lanzamiento.

items.q: What does the team hope to have achieved by noon?
items.e: 'By noon, the team hopes to have reached its first five hundred downloads'.

Two thousand subscribers: dos mil es la cantidad de suscriptores a los que se envía el anuncio, no el objetivo de descargas.
A new office: no se menciona ninguna oficina nueva.

items.q: What advice did the manager give?
o: Rest and turn off phones tonight
items.a: Rest and turn off phones tonight
items.e: 'turn off your phones and get a good night's sleep'.

Work late to prepare: el manager dijo lo contrario: no trabajar hasta tarde.
Meet friends for dinner: la cena con la amiga es el plan de Lucía, no un consejo del manager.

items.q: What does the text suggest about Lucía?
o: She will probably check the servers several times before sleeping
items.a: She will probably check the servers several times before sleeping
items.e: 'by the time she goes to bed, she will have checked the servers at least three times'.

She will cancel her dinner: va a cenar con su amiga e intentará relajarse.

title: The future of office work
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text: Experts believe that by 2035 computers will have taken over many routine office tasks, but that does not mean that most people will be unemployed. History suggests otherwise: when factories introduced machines, new professions appeared that nobody had imagined. However, workers who are unlikely to adapt quickly may find the transition difficult. That is why some companies are already offering training courses, which are due to begin next year. Analysts warn that those who wait until the changes have arrived will find it much harder to catch up, and they recommend that employees start learning new skills now, while there is still time to prepare.

items.q: According to the text, what does history suggest?
o: Most people will lose their jobs
New professions will appear as technology changes
items.a: New professions will appear as technology changes
items.e: 'when factories introduced machines, new professions appeared'.

Most people will lose their jobs: el texto dice que las máquinas tomen tareas no significa que la mayoría quede sin empleo.
Machines never replace workers: dice que los ordenadores asumirán muchas tareas rutinarias; sí reemplazan algunas.
Companies avoid training: dice lo contrario: algunas empresas ya ofrecen cursos.

o: People who wait for the changes to arrive will find it harder to catch up
items.a: People who wait for the changes to arrive will find it harder to catch up
items.e: 'those who wait until the changes have arrived will find it much harder to catch up'.

Training courses will be cancelled: los cursos empezarán el año próximo; no se habla de cancelarlos.
Machines will stop working: no se menciona que las máquinas dejen de funcionar.
Nobody will need offices: no se dice eso; habla de nuevas habilidades.
